eyebrow: AI Engineering Leadership & Architecture · Chapter Four
titlePlain: Turning Business Goals Into a Technical
subtitle: Lesson 19 · Roadmapping

eyebrow: The business goal, as handed down
code:
"Reduce customer support costs by 20% this year,
primarily by deflecting more tickets to the AI
assistant before they reach a human agent."

Real and meaningful -- and zero technical specifics.
caption: Turning this into an actual roadmap is the Staff/Principal engineer's job.

eyebrow: Breaking the goal into technical initiatives
code:
1. Improve retrieval quality (chunking, hybrid search)
2. Expand knowledge base to unanswerable categories
3. Confidence threshold -- route low-confidence to human
4. Reduce response latency
5. [Tech debt] Refactor prompt-assembly logic (L18) --
   unblocks #1's hybrid-search work
caption: Initiative 5 wasn't asked for -- it's on the roadmap because it's a real dependency.

eyebrow: Sequencing: the hardest and most valuable part
code:
#5 (refactor) BEFORE #1 (hybrid search) --
  hybrid search touches the exact code the refactor
  cleans up. Build on top of it now, pay 5x the cost.

#3 (confidence threshold) CAN run in parallel --
  no shared dependency with #1 or #5.
caption: Listing initiatives is easy. Figuring out the order is the real planning work.

eyebrow: This chapter's own tools become roadmap inputs
code:
Capacity planning (L3)  -> will #2 hit an infra ceiling?
Build-vs-buy (L7, L10)  -> build hybrid search, or adopt
                           a vendor's retrieval features?
Tech-debt math (L18)    -> justifies #5's place on the
                           roadmap with no direct metric.
caption: Roadmapping is where every other skill in this course gets applied together.
